brief.analysis: The engine's own trend-versus-flat-mean readings openly disagree by more than the usual margin, which is direct evidence the 'normal' level for defense-versus-market is drifting upward — consistent with the global step-up in military budgets that has re-rated the sector. None of the three moving-average checks confirm a turn, the historical hit rate is a coin flip, and the nearer target has essentially already been reached. Shorting defense back to an old average that is itself rising is betting against a structural spending shift.
brief.report_line: We are flagged short aerospace-and-defense versus the market, but we advise against it: the signal's own trend measure shows the normal level drifting up alongside rising global defense budgets, so the old average is a moving — and likely invalid — target.

brief.analysis: This bets chipmakers give back their lead over the broader Nasdaq, but that lead is being driven by the AI build-out — a multi-year spending wave that has permanently lifted how much chips are worth relative to everything else, so the old five-year average is very likely no longer the right target. There is no sign the snap-back has even started: the ratio is still far from any target, only one of three moving-average checks confirms, and the medium-term trend has not rolled over. Shorting semis-over-Nasdaq here is fighting the strongest structural tailwind in the market.
brief.report_line: We are flagged short semiconductors versus the Nasdaq on a stretched-relationship signal, but we advise against it: the AI-spending boom has likely reset the normal relationship higher, and the reversion hasn't begun.

brief.analysis: The real regime worry is that central banks buy gold but never silver, structurally supporting gold and holding this silver-to-gold relationship elevated, while booming solar and electronics demand gives silver its own durable floor gold lacks. But the trade has already largely worked — the extreme stretch has collapsed and the first target has been hit — so the flat five-year average below current levels is the questionable part, not the recent move. Tradeable as a finish to a move already made, but size it down: pushing all the way to the old average fights a genuine change in silver demand.
brief.report_line: We are short silver versus gold; the sharp snap-back has already reached its first target, so we would take profits toward that level rather than chase the old five-year average, which structural silver demand may have moved permanently higher.

brief.analysis: Metals-and-mining has surged on the same forces lifting the precious-metals complex — heavy central-bank gold buying and industrial silver and copper demand — which is a real structural tailwind under the sector, not just a spike. That said, the extreme stretch has already collapsed toward normal, the first target is met, all three moving-average checks confirm a turn, and the trend-adjusted reading shows the underlying mean has barely drifted. Tradeable as a finishing move, but the thin history and live commodity boom argue for a reduced size rather than a full-conviction short.
brief.report_line: We are short metals-and-miners versus the market; most of the reversion is already behind us and the technicals confirm, so we would run it small toward the remaining target given the ongoing commodity boom underneath the sector.
